production.note: Calendar years, as in the Venom F5 and Bugatti records (Hennessey publishes no US model years). Quote (Hennessey, 19 January 2017): "Since 2010 Hennessey Performance has built twelve road-going Venom GT's" "along with one prototype for a total production of thirteen vehicles", and "Production of the world's fastest hardtop coupe and convertible has now officially concluded." The Final Edition car was completed in January 2017.

body.note: "The first six Venoms were all hardtops and the last 6 were roadsters." The open car is the Venom GT Spyder, sold under its own name; this record is the coupe.

fuel.note: Inferred: Hennessey describes a conventional twin-turbo petrol V8 with no hybrid system.

powerHp.note: Quote (venomgt.com spec table, headed "2014 Hennessey Venom GT Specifications"): "1244 bhp @ 6600 rpm (cockpit-adjustable to 800, 1000 & 1244 bhp)". Hennessey states bhp with no SAE certification, so powerStandard is Other, as for the Venom F5. The rating changed over the run: "power grew from 1,000 bhp to an astounding 1,451 bhp", and the 2016-2017 Final Edition is "powered by the same twin turbo 7.0 Liter V8 engine producing 1,451 bhp" (venomgt-final-edition). The 1,244 bhp rating is the one on Hennessey's permanent specification page, with a matching curb weight.

weightLb.note: Quote (venomgt.com spec table, Dimensions & Capacities, Curb weight): "2743 lb/1244 kg". 2014 specification; single configuration (Ricardo 6-speed manual).

sources.title: The Venom GT - 2014 Hennessey Venom GT Specifications
Hennessey Venom GT Final Edition Crosses the Finish Line (January 19, 2017)

discrepancies.reason: The rating rose over the run: Hennessey says "power grew from 1,000 bhp to an astounding 1,451 bhp", and the 2016-2017 Final Edition (3 cars) is "producing 1,451 bhp".
discrepancies.resolution: Used 1,244 bhp from the 2014 specification page, the only Hennessey page that pairs a rating with a curb weight; the run is 13 cars, too few and too varied for year-split records.
